description.short_caption: Chronic ulcerated lesion on the finger.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a chronic, irregularly shaped ulcerated lesion on the dorsal aspect of a finger. The lesion has raised, erythematous borders and a central area of granulation tissue with some crusting. The surrounding skin appears mildly erythematous but otherwise intact. The lesion's chronicity is suggested by its well-defined borders and granulation tissue.

description.short_caption: Erythematous and crusted skin lesion on the finger after 1 month of treatment.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up view of a finger and adjacent web space with erythematous, scaly, and crusted lesions. The affected area appears inflamed, with some regions of desquamation and crusting. The surrounding skin shows mild erythema, and there is no visible purulence or ulceration. The lesions suggest a chronic or subacute inflammatory process, possibly infectious or dermatologic in nature.

The lesion's appearance suggests partial resolution, consistent with ongoing treatment.
